legend.title: Legend of diagram symbols
legend.valley: Blue dashed line: fold towards you (valley fold).
legend.mountain: Red dash-dotted line: fold away from you (mountain fold).
legend.arrow: Blue arrow: direction of this step's fold.
legend.front: Filled black circle with the letter F: front side of the paper.
legend.back: Hollow hatched circle with the letter V: back side of the paper.
legend.up: The arrow in the top right corner shows the top of the paper.

home.heroSub: Learn to fold paper with detailed, accessible, bilingual instructions. One single website for blind people, people with low vision, and sighted people.
home.whatText: OrigamiECJ is a project by the team Eu Concego Jogar (ECJ) that teaches origami accessibly. Every tutorial has step-by-step instructions that can be followed without looking at the images, with detailed spatial guidance, diagram descriptions, and fixes for common mistakes.

features.title: Instructions that do not depend on sight
features.text: Each step explains the paper position, orientation, what moves, the fold direction, the expected result, and common mistakes.

features.title: High-contrast diagrams
features.text: SVG diagrams use dashed lines for valley folds, dash-dotted lines for mountain folds, and direction arrows, with a legend.

features.title: Bilingual
features.text: The website is available in Brazilian Portuguese and English, with language switching at any time.

features.title: Local progress
features.text: Your progress is saved in your browser, with no account and no data being sent anywhere.

features.title: Works with keyboard and screen readers
features.text: The whole website is keyboard-navigable and compatible with NVDA, VoiceOver, and TalkBack.

features.title: Responsive
features.text: The website works on small screens and supports zoom up to 200% without losing content.

home.modelsText: Start with the simple models, with complete and accessible instructions.
home.a11yText: Everyone uses the same interface. There is no separate version for blind people: accessibility is part of the core structure of the website.
home.progressText: OrigamiECJ only saves tutorial progress in the browser's local storage, on your device. We do not collect personal data, do not use tracking, and do not send data to third parties.

about.title: About OrigamiECJ
about.intro: OrigamiECJ is a project by the team Eu Concego Jogar (ECJ), created so that anyone can learn origami — including blind people and people with low vision — using the same interface.

sections.title: Why an accessible origami website?
paragraphs: Origami is a visual art: most tutorials depend on diagrams. Blind people are left out because the instructions say 'fold like in the picture' or 'turn it over' without explaining what that means.

OrigamiECJ rewrites each fold in words. Each step states the paper position, the spatial orientation, the tip or edge that moves, the fold direction, the expected result, the common mistake, and how to fix it.
Everyone uses the same interface. There is no separate version for blind people: accessibility is part of the core structure.

sections.title: How the tutorials are written
paragraphs: Each model has a step-by-step script, with texts in Portuguese and English, high-contrast diagrams with a legend, and a text description of each diagram.
The instructions can be followed without seeing the images. Diagrams help those who see, and the descriptions help those who do not — and everyone learns together.

sections.title: Privacy
paragraphs: The website does not require registration, does not collect personal data, does not use tracking, and does not send data to third parties.
Tutorial progress is saved only in the browser's local storage, on your device. You can erase it at any time.

credits.title: Credits
credits.projectCredit: OrigamiECJ is a project by the team Eu Concego Jogar (ECJ).
credits.contactText: For questions, suggestions, or partnerships, write to euconcego@gmail.com.
credits.modelsText: The initial models (paper dart, paper cup, and paper boat) are traditional origami folds in the public domain. The instructions, texts, and diagrams are original creations by the ECJ team.
credits.origamiDbText: OrigamiECJ consults the origami-db database as a technical reference for crease patterns and 3D folded models. We do not copy data, images, instructions, or models from that database.
credits.origamiDbLicense: origami-db is published under the GPL-3.0 license, by dozingpip. Official address:
credits.techText: The website is built with semantic HTML, organized CSS, and modular JavaScript, with no external dependencies and no data collection.
credits.licenseText: The project code is distributed under the MIT license, unless otherwise indicated. Text content and diagrams are creations of the ECJ team.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.intro: OrigamiECJ was built following WCAG 2.1 (level AA) guidelines and accessibility best practices. See below the features and how to test them.

sections.title: Keyboard and focus
paragraphs: The whole website can be used with the keyboard alone. Focus is always visible and follows a logical navigation order.
Press Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move back, and Enter to activate buttons and links. The Esc key closes dialogs and menus.

sections.title: Screen readers
paragraphs: The website was tested to work with NVDA, VoiceOver, and TalkBack.
Headings have a correct hierarchy, all controls have accessible names, and important changes are announced by aria-live regions.
The tutorial announces the current step and the total number of steps, and each diagram has a title and an equivalent text description.

sections.title: Contrast and color
paragraphs: Texts have adequate contrast. Diagrams do not rely only on color: each fold type also has a different line pattern (dashed for valley, dash-dotted for mountain).

sections.title: Zoom and small screens
paragraphs: The website supports zoom up to 200% without losing content and works on small screens with a responsive layout.

sections.title: Motion and animations
paragraphs: The website respects the system preference for reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion).
Any animation can be paused with the 'Pause animations' button, available on the whole website.

sections.title: Not relying on a single form of information
paragraphs: No information is conveyed only by color, image, position, or sound.
Every diagram has an equivalent text description and every visual piece of information has a text alternative.

testingList: Language switching preserving the current step.
No exclusive reliance on color or image.

help.title: Help
help.intro: Find answers to the most common questions about OrigamiECJ.

sections.title: How do I start a tutorial?
paragraphs: Open the model catalog, choose a model, and press 'Start the tutorial'. The first step appears with the complete instructions.

sections.title: Do I need to see the diagrams?
paragraphs: No. Each step has a complete text description, written to be followed without looking at the images. The diagrams are extra support.

sections.title: What do the lines in the diagram mean?
paragraphs: A blue dashed line is a fold towards you (valley). A red dash-dotted line is a fold away from you (mountain). The arrow shows the direction of the movement. The full legend is below the first diagram.

sections.title: How do I switch the language?
paragraphs: Use the language button at the top of the website. The website detects your browser language automatically and keeps your choice while you navigate.

sections.title: Where is my progress saved?
paragraphs: Progress is saved in your browser's local storage, on your device. No account is needed and no data is sent to servers. You can erase your progress at any time.

sections.title: How do I pause animations?
paragraphs: Use the 'Pause animations' button at the top of the website. The website also respects the reduced-motion preference configured in your system.

sections.title: Does the website collect my data?
paragraphs: No. The website does not require registration, does not collect personal data, does not use tracking, and does not send data to third parties.
